pathway.title: Elanco Animal Health Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid, and it is still high. Net debt of USD 3,388 million is 4.38x reported and 3.36x adjusted EBITDA, against the 3.1x the issuer reports, which leaves out the USD 255 million headquarters finance lease. Adjusted net leverage fell by 0.50x in the half-year, about four fifths of it from higher EBITDA, while the issuer repaid USD 89 million of borrowings and paid USD 76 million in cash for AHV. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C18

- Refinancing the 2028 maturities is the central credit test. On the 2025 year-end schedule, scheduled principal is USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, then USD 1,236 million in 2028 and USD 548 million in 2029. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million covers the 2028 amount 1.04x and the two years together only 0.72x, and the USD 750 million unsecured senior notes fall due on 2028-08-28, so the market window is 2027, the year Seresto loses its United States formulation patent. Management's target of at least USD 1,000 million of free cash flow over 2026 to 2028, on its own definition, would cover only 56.05% of the 2028 and 2029 maturities even if all of it were retained, so refinancing is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C26

- Revenue durability is the main business risk and the test has already started, which corrects the earlier Business & governance review. That review treated a United States generic Seresto entrant as a possible future event, but the 2025 annual report states that a competitor began selling a generic product competitive with the Seresto collar in January 2026, more than a year before certain patent rights expire, and that Seresto has had no patent protection in certain markets since 2025. Seresto and Advantage Family together supplied USD 593 million, or 21.65%, of half-year revenue and earn about 70% and 60% of their annual revenue in the first half, so the 2027 flea-and-tick season is the real test. The filings give no 2025 quarterly Seresto revenue, so erosion cannot yet be measured. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_elanco-20260331exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C22

- New-product volume is carrying earnings, and the guidance implies the pace will slow. Half-year volume grew 7% and price 2%, led by Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and adjusted EBITDA rose 21.01% with 35.41% of the extra revenue reaching adjusted EBITDA. Full-year guidance of USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million implies second-half adjusted EBITDA of USD 388 million to USD 413 million against USD 387 million a year earlier, growth of only 0.26% to 6.72%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C16

- Debt service is covered, but cover is flat because interest is rising. FY2025 cash interest cover was 3.28x reported and 4.37x adjusted, and on income-statement interest the last-twelve-months cover is 4.07x adjusted against 4.10x for FY2025, so earnings growth is being absorbed by a 31.82% rise in half-year net interest expense. On an analyst estimate, about USD 1,489 million of floating-rate debt would be left unhedged after the swap roll scheduled for August 2026, adding USD 14.89 million a year for each percentage point, while free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months covers the USD 63 million of scheduled principal 6.02x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C05; calculation C12

- Claims outside the debt figure add obligations that the leverage ratios do not show. The liability for the royalty sale is USD 315 million at an 18.3% effective rate, AHV carries USD 100 million of deferred cash and contingent consideration of USD 67 million at fair value, the restructuring reserve is USD 86 million and the headquarters lease ends with a USD 250 million purchase option in 2030. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

- Behaviour is creditor-aligned but legal capacity is unproven, and management is signalling a change in posture once leverage falls. The 2024 aqua sale proceeds of USD 1,294 million went mainly to term loans and no dividends are planned, yet the issuer says reaching leverage below 3x next year will unlock greater capital allocation flexibility, although it also states a long-term leverage target of 2.0x to 2.5x, and without the credit agreement the limits on payments to shareholders are not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20; calculation C26

- Asset protection rests on franchise value, not tangible assets. Goodwill and other intangibles of USD 8,049 million are 59.35% of total assets, which leaves tangible equity negative at USD 1,461 million, and a goodwill impairment of USD 1,042 million in 2023 and a USD 47 million product impairment in 2025 show that franchise value can erode. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

cells.text: One reportable segment: pet health and farm animal products, about 200 brands, sold in more than 90 countries
Parasiticides (Advantage Family, Seresto, Credelio Family), dermatology (Zenrelia), vaccines (Tru Family), pain (Galliprant); 48.78% of FY2025 revenue
Medicated feed additives, injectable antibiotics, vaccines, insecticides and enzymes for cattle, poultry, swine and sheep (Rumensin, Experior, Maxiban and Monteban); 50.10% of FY2025 revenue

Pet products to distributors, retailers and veterinarians; farm products to distributors and producers; largest customer about 12% of revenue, second about 7%; sales force of over 2,200 representatives
16 own sites and about 140 contract manufacturers; dual sources for key active ingredients; biologics active ingredients made mainly in-house; Kansas City site to close by end of 2026
368 in FY2025 (7.80% of revenue); over 1,000 people in research, development and regulatory affairs; Monheim animal studies unit to close by end of 2026
Zoetis, Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health and Merck Animal Health, plus generics and nutritional producers; competes on quality, price, effectiveness and new products
About 7,000 patents and applications in over 95 countries; Seresto U.S. formulation patent expires September 2027; some principal products have no patent protection
About 70% of Seresto and 60% of Advantage Family revenue falls in the first half; first-half revenue was 51.62% of FY2025 revenue
New products (Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro, Befrena launched in 2026) and AHV; Management Language: innovation revenue target of 1,250 for 2026
2025 Restructuring Plan; Management Language: Elanco Ascend targets 200 to 250 of adjusted EBITDA savings by 2030

runs.text: - Strength: pet and livestock exposure is balanced, with Pet Health at 48.78% and Farm Animal at 50.10% of FY2025 revenue and the United States at 47.38%, so weakness in discretionary pet spending and weakness in livestock markets are separate exposures, which supports cash flow visibility and debt service through a cycle. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: new products are replacing eroding franchises, with half-year volume growth of 7%, innovation revenue of USD 892 million in FY2025 against a 2026 target of USD 1,250 million, and research spending at 6.90% of revenue, which supports revenue durability and the margin mix; the targets are management language. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; calculation C22; calculation C23

- Strength: financial behaviour has favoured creditors, with USD 1,294 million of aqua sale proceeds applied mainly to term loans, no dividends planned and the 2027 term loan refinanced into facilities due 2029 to 2032, which lowers refinancing risk before 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20

- Strength: near-term amortisation is light and covered, with USD 63 million of scheduled principal in each of 2026 and 2027 against USD 379 million of last-twelve-months free cash flow, and an undrawn USD 750 million revolver due in 2029, which limits liquidity risk until 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C02

- Weakness: leverage is still high and interest cover is flat, with net debt of USD 3,388 million at 3.36x adjusted and 4.38x reported EBITDA, accrual cover of 4.07x and FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 676 million well below the adjusted USD 901 million, so little cushion exists if earnings slip. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C10

- Weakness: revenue is concentrated in a handful of products and one channel, with five products at about 38% of revenue, one distributor at about 12% and a live generic competitor to Seresto, which exposes price, volume and receivables to a single decision or product. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

- Weakness: the 2028 maturities of USD 1,236 million and 2029 maturities of USD 548 million together exceed liquidity of USD 1,280 million, with 79.67% of principal secured and floating, so a closed market in 2027 would force asset-backed or higher-cost funding. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C04

- Weakness: debt-like claims outside the debt figure and a thin tangible base, with USD 315 million of royalty liability, USD 250 million of lease option and goodwill and intangibles at 59.35% of assets, reduce cash available to creditors and the protection beyond franchise value. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C14

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The October 2025 refinancing is the issuer's one new debt issue in the period. On 2025-10-31 it entered a Term Loan B due 2032 of USD 1,100 million at Term SOFR plus 1.75%, a Euro Term Loan due 2029 of EUR 400 million at EURIBOR plus a leverage-based spread and an Incremental Term Facility due 2032 of USD 540 million at Term SOFR plus 2.25%, for aggregate gross proceeds of USD 2,106 million, and repaid the USD 2,102 million Term Loan B due 2027 in full with those proceeds and cash on hand. The new term loans amortise at 0.25% a quarter, 1.875% a quarter and 0.25% a quarter, and mature on 2032-10-31, 2029-04-30 and 2032-10-31. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 109–110; calculation C11

Earlier financing moves were the Incremental Term Facility due 2031 of USD 350 million in August 2024, the extension of the revolver to July 2029 in July 2024 and the extension of the securitization facility to June 2028 on 2025-06-25. The sale of future revenue to Blackstone funds in May 2025 raised USD 295 million, USD 290 million after transaction costs, against U.S. royalties and milestones on XDEMVY to 2033-08-24, and the issuer used the proceeds to repay debt. The Indianapolis headquarters finance lease, which began in June 2025, carries a USD 250 million purchase option or landlord put at the end of its five-year term. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; calculation C12

The AHV International acquisition closed on 2026-04-30 for total purchase consideration of USD 243 million: USD 76 million in cash at closing, USD 100 million of deferred cash through 2030 and contingent consideration valued at USD 67 million, with up to USD 140 million payable on milestones through 2032. The issuer funded the closing from cash and a securitization draw of USD 50 million on 2026-04-22 that it repaid before the quarter ended, and says the deal is not expected to materially affect its deleveraging timeline, which is a management statement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-03-31_elan-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C10

No new bond, loan or sponsor-backed issue after the October 2025 refinancing is described in the filings supplied up to 2026-08-05, and no third-quarter 2026 report is in the set, so later issues are not established. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.value: The main definition risk is the debt perimeter. The issuer's net debt of USD 3,159 million leaves out the USD 255 million headquarters finance lease that the balance sheet carries inside debt and starts from debt before USD 26 million of issuance costs, so counting the lease puts net debt USD 229 million higher and adjusted net leverage at 3.36x against 3.13x on the issuer's own inputs, which it prints as 3.1x.

fields.value: The source inventory in Source readiness agrees with these figures and lists no executed credit agreement, indenture, rating report or third-quarter 2026 report. Period risks follow. FY2024 reported EBITDA of USD 1,385 million includes the USD 640 million gain on the aqua sale, so FY2024 reported leverage is not a clean base; the half-year to 2026-06-30 includes AHV for two months; and last-twelve-months EBITDA is built from reported components with a USD 1 million rounding gap to the issuer's own adjusted figure. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading Elanco as slow to deleverage is operating momentum: reported revenue growth of 12.53% in the half-year, an issuer adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.9% against 21.2% a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 206 million against USD 111 million. If that pace holds, EBITDA growth alone moves adjusted net leverage toward the issuer's year-end target of about 3.0x without debt repayment, although part of the revenue growth is AHV and currency rather than organic.

fields.value: Business and governance review of Elanco Animal Health Inc (Elanco) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway, covering business model, ownership, governance and behaviour, transactions and operating drivers from the filings supplied. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco shows no documented shareholder extraction and no identified controlling holder, so creditor risk sits in business durability: five product lines supply about 38% of revenue, one distributor about 12%, and the Seresto collar loses its United States formulation patent in September 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is rated medium because the evidence is incomplete, not adverse: the proxy statement, credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so board independence, ownership percentages and legal capacity for distributions or priming are not established. Behaviour so far is creditor-aligned, with divestiture proceeds applied to term debt, no dividends and a longer maturity profile, though other financing claims have grown: a USD 295 million royalty sale, a headquarters lease with a USD 250 million purchase option and deferred and contingent payments for the April 2026 AHV acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings depend on a handful of product lines and one channel partner rather than on any segment or country. Five products and product families supplied about 38% of FY2025 revenue, the Advantage Family alone about 10%, and the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12%, with a second distributor at about 7%. The same customer owed USD 131 million at 2026-06-30, about 12.16% of receivables, so a change in that distributor's ordering or payment terms would move cash flow quickly.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability is weakest where patent cover is ending. The Seresto formulation patent expires in the United States in September 2027, its European formulation patents expired in June 2025, with supplementary protection certificates in some countries running to August 2026, and certain Advantage Family products, Rumensin and Maxiban and Monteban have no patent protection. Volume growth of 7% in the half-year to 2026-06-30 came from new products, led by Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, so creditors are relying on launches replacing eroding franchises.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Litigation is extensive but has not produced a recorded liability. A securities class action over Zenrelia safety, labelling and launch disclosures was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-03-26 and is on appeal, the related derivative suits are stayed, and the Tevra antitrust verdict for the issuer was affirmed on 2026-07-06; the issuer states it has established no material liability for these matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern about concentration is momentum from new products: second-quarter organic constant-currency revenue growth of 8%, innovation revenue of USD 892 million in FY2025 against a raised 2026 target of USD 1,250 million, and Zenrelia described by the issuer as a blockbuster in the year to July. If these launches keep volume growth near the 7% of the half-year, the Seresto expiry is more likely to be absorbed than to be a cliff, which is an analyst interpretation. The view would change toward higher risk if volume growth fades before September 2027, if a generic Seresto entrant appears in the United States, or if the largest distributor shifts volume; it would change toward lower risk if the proxy statement and legal documents confirm independent directors, no holder above five percent and tight limits on distributions and priming.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Elanco Animal Health Inc (Elanco) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway, combining the financial foundation and the business and governance review with the filings supplied. Figures are in USD millions unless stated and the latest balance sheet is dated 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco is an adequate but stretched credit that is improving: adjusted net leverage has fallen to 3.36x mainly on higher earnings, yet liquidity of USD 1,280 million only just covers the USD 1,236 million due in 2028, so the 2027 refinancing is the test. A competitor has sold a generic Seresto collar in the United States since January 2026, so revenue durability, not near-term debt service, is the main business risk.

fields.value: - Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid, and it is still high. Net debt of USD 3,388 million is 4.38x reported and 3.36x adjusted EBITDA, against the 3.1x the issuer reports, which leaves out the USD 255 million headquarters finance lease. Adjusted net leverage fell by 0.50x in the half-year, about four fifths of it from higher EBITDA, while the issuer repaid USD 89 million of borrowings and paid USD 76 million in cash for AHV.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing the 2028 maturities is the central credit test. On the 2025 year-end schedule, scheduled principal is USD 63 million in each of 2026 and 2027, then USD 1,236 million in 2028 and USD 548 million in 2029. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million covers the 2028 amount 1.04x and the two years together only 0.72x, and the USD 750 million unsecured senior notes fall due on 2028-08-28, so the market window is 2027, the year Seresto loses its United States formulation patent. Management's target of at least USD 1,000 million of free cash flow over 2026 to 2028, on its own definition, would cover only 56.05% of the 2028 and 2029 maturities even if all of it were retained, so refinancing is needed.

fields.value: - Revenue durability is the main business risk and the test has already started, which corrects the earlier Business & governance review. That review treated a United States generic Seresto entrant as a possible future event, but the 2025 annual report states that a competitor began selling a generic product competitive with the Seresto collar in January 2026, more than a year before certain patent rights expire, and that Seresto has had no patent protection in certain markets since 2025. Seresto and Advantage Family together supplied USD 593 million, or 21.65%, of half-year revenue and earn about 70% and 60% of their annual revenue in the first half, so the 2027 flea-and-tick season is the real test. The filings give no 2025 quarterly Seresto revenue, so erosion cannot yet be measured.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is momentum and the pace of deleveraging. Half-year adjusted EBITDA rose 21.01%, the issuer reports share gains for Zenrelia and Credelio Quattro, and its year-end target of about 3.0x needs only about USD 91.50 million less issuer net debt at the guidance midpoint, against USD 173 million of free cash flow in the second half of 2025. Guidance has been raised twice since February: the 2026 adjusted EBITDA range was USD 955 million to USD 985 million in February, USD 975 million to USD 1,005 million in May and is now USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million, so the slower second-half growth it implies may simply be conservative. Cash taxes rose to USD 225 million in 2025 mainly because of tax payments on the aqua sale gain, so FY2025 free cash flow likely understated the run rate, although the size of the one-off part is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco sells animal health products in more than 90 countries through one reportable segment, with Pet Health at 48.78% of FY2025 revenue (parasiticides, dermatology, vaccines and pain) and Farm Animal at 50.10% (feed additives, antibiotics, vaccines and enzymes for cattle, poultry, swine and sheep). Sales go through veterinary distributors, retailers and directly to producers, and the sections read give no contract duration or renewal rates, so revenue visibility rests on prescribing habits, brands and seasonal demand rather than on contracted backlog. For creditors, balanced end markets and a regulated animal-health product set support cash flow, while first-half seasonality, with 51.62% of FY2025 revenue arriving in the first half, makes cash and working capital swing within the year and makes the first half the season that decides the full-year debt service picture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Elanco is a listed Indiana corporation separated from Eli Lilly in 2019, with no sponsor and no controlling holder identified; holders above five percent, board independence and related-person dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The credit facilities are secured by a significant part of the group's assets and the 2028 notes are senior unsecured, so the structure ranks the notes behind secured lenders to the extent of the collateral, and the annual report says a default under the credit facilities could stop payments on the notes through a cash sweep; guarantor scope and the priority among secured facilities are not established. Financial policy so far has favoured creditors: no dividends are anticipated, although the policy may change at any time, the facilities restrict dividends, debt and liens, and the aqua proceeds repaid term loans. The offsetting signals are the issuer's statement that leverage below 3x unlocks greater capital allocation flexibility, the growth in claims outside the debt figure and the annual report's reference to activist shareholders as a risk to strategy; the governance risk level from Business & governance is medium because the evidence is incomplete rather than adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring and seasonal, moderately cyclical and concentrated, with no disclosed contract backlog. Price added 2% and volume 5% to FY2025 revenue growth of 6% after a 2% drag from the aqua sale, and in the half-year to 2026-06-30 volume added 7% and price 2%, led by Zenrelia, Credelio Quattro and AdTab with part of the volume from new customers. Growth that depends on launches is only as durable as clinic adoption of each product, so the credit implication is that earnings rest on the pipeline continuing to replace franchises that are losing protection. Concentration adds fragility: five products and families supply about 38% of revenue, the largest customer, an affiliate of Cencora, about 12% and the second distributor about 7%, and the same largest customer owed USD 131 million, 12.16% of receivables, at 2026-06-30, so a change in one distributor's ordering or payment terms would move revenue and cash quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is modest. Price added 2% in both periods, and the annual report warns that generic competition may force lower prices, discounts or rebates; sales rebates and discounts were a liability of USD 450 million at 2026-06-30 and the auditor treats United States rebate estimates as a critical audit matter, so a change in accruals would move revenue and cash. Farm Animal revenue is exposed to regulation and consumer sentiment: shared-class antibiotics were 9% and animal-only antibiotics 15% of FY2025 revenue, with 89% of the animal-only amount from ionophores, and the European Union has restricted preventative antibiotic use since 2022. Revenue is not structurally declining on the evidence, with reported half-year growth of 12.53% and second-quarter organic constant-currency growth of 8%, but the Seresto exposure described in the key findings is the clearest case of a franchise that is already facing substitution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure but not against a sharp loss of parasiticide revenue. Gross margin was 55.0% in FY2025 against 54.9% in FY2024, with price and productivity offset by inflation and higher manufacturing costs, and 57.79% in the half-year against 57.40%, helped by mix and price despite higher inventory costs; the issuer guides adjusted gross margin to 55.2% to 55.6% for 2026. In the half-year 35.41% of the extra revenue reached adjusted EBITDA, which is operating leverage on the way up. The reverse follows on the way down: gross profit is 57.79% of revenue, so each USD 100 million of lost revenue removes about USD 57.79 million of gross profit, while selling costs of USD 830 million grew 12.01%, nearly as fast as revenue, partly to support launches and higher pay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is real but arrives after the cash cost. The 2025 restructuring plan carries about USD 116 million of cash severance before savings of about USD 25 million in 2026 and USD 60 million in 2027, and the Elanco Ascend programme targets USD 200 million to USD 250 million of adjusted EBITDA savings by 2030; all of these savings are management estimates. Input inflation is passing through inventory into cost of sales, and tariffs are a small and uncertain item: an April 2026 proclamation on imported patented pharmaceuticals carves out certain animal-health products and is not expected to apply to the issuer until at least September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion of EBITDA into free cash flow is moderate and improving. Free cash flow was USD 394 million in FY2024 and USD 284 million in FY2025, which is 42.01% of reported and 31.52% of adjusted EBITDA for FY2025, and USD 379 million over the last twelve months, or 37.56% of adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 was held down by capital spending of USD 276 million, 5.85% of revenue against 3.31% in FY2024, for the Elwood antibody plant, and by cash taxes that rose to USD 225 million from USD 140 million, mainly on the aqua sale gain; the last-twelve-months capital spending ratio is 4.74% after half-year spending fell to USD 84 million from USD 122 million on timing. The half-year absorbed USD 239 million of working capital as receivables rose to USD 1,077 million from USD 873 million, which should unwind in the second half if collections follow the usual seasonal pattern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending flexibility over the maturity wall is not established, because maintenance and growth spending are not split. The Elwood expansion and two early-stage projects suspended in 2025 suggest that part of the spending is discretionary. Against that, the headquarters lease adds payments of about USD 17 million a year and a USD 250 million purchase option in 2030, and restructuring cash (the reserve is USD 86 million) and USD 100 million of deferred AHV cash must be paid first. The credit implication is that free cash flow supports the scheduled principal of USD 63 million a year easily, 6.02x, but does not by itself build liquidity to meet the USD 1,784 million due across 2028 and 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rivalry is intense and is the force most likely to change credit quality. Zoetis, Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health and Merck Animal Health compete on quality, price, effectiveness and new products, and a generic Seresto competitor has sold in the United States since January 2026. Price and volume pressure in parasiticides would cut the high-margin earnings that fund debt service; the issuer reports Zenrelia up 9 percentage points in United States JAK share and Credelio Quattro in more than half of United States clinics, but these are management-reported gains, not independent measures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The threat of new entrants is low for new prescription and biologic franchises, because regulatory approvals, a patent portfolio of about seven thousand patents and applications and specialised manufacturing take years, but it is real for off-patent products: certain Advantage Family products, Rumensin and Maxiban and Monteban have no patent protection, Seresto has none in certain markets, and start-up companies compete in the sector. For creditors, entry is the route by which eroding franchises lose price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Substitutes are generics and lower-cost alternatives. The annual report says generics may be viewed as more cost-effective, that veterinarians may favour lower-cost options when pet owners face financial pressure and that farm customers may trade down when feed and protein costs move, and mass retailers are being added, with Costco and Dollar General joining in the first quarter of 2026. Substitution shows up as rebates and discounts rather than lost volume at first, which lowers net price and cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Buyer power is meaningful. The largest distributor is about 12% of revenue and the second about 7%, the rebate liability is USD 450 million, and the filings list changes in distributor inventory among the causes of revenue variation, so quarterly revenue can overstate or understate end demand. A shift in one distributor's volumes would hit cash through receivables first.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supplier power is contained but not absent. Key materials are typically available from more than one source, although in certain instances they come from a single source, chemically derived active ingredients are bought from external partners and biologic ingredients are made mainly in house. The 2024 administration of the contract manufacturer TriRx Speke led to a USD 15 million impairment and a USD 36 million purchase of the Speke site, which shows that supply failures turn into capital spending and charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Regulation and policy are material because approvals, labels and restrictions can remove or limit revenue quickly. In 2024 the FDA required a boxed safety warning on the Zenrelia label, and the issuer now describes Zenrelia as the largest contributor to second-quarter growth, while a securities class action over its disclosures is on appeal; antibiotic products were about 24% of FY2025 revenue and are the most exposed to restrictions; tariffs have so far been carved out for animal-health products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Economic factors are currency, rates and customer finances. About 52% of half-year revenue is in foreign currencies, foreign exchange added 3% to half-year growth and the issuer expects a revenue tailwind of about USD 60 million in 2026 that can reverse; floating-rate debt, with interest rate swaps of USD 2,300 million scheduled to mature in August 2026, makes cash interest sensitive to rates; and pet-owner finances and farm input costs shape demand for discretionary and farm products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Social and technology factors work through the product mix. Consumer sentiment against antibiotic use in protein weighs on parts of Farm Animal, and adoption of the methane-reducing Bovaer has been tempered by the absence of government incentives. Growth is concentrated in new classes, JAK inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies and combination parasiticides, which need continued research spending of 6.90% of revenue to keep the replacement pipeline full.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: balanced pet and livestock revenue, new products replacing eroding franchises, creditor-aligned financial behaviour with extended maturities, and light scheduled principal to 2028 backed by free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months.

fields.value: - Weaknesses: net debt of USD 3,388 million at 3.36x adjusted EBITDA with flat interest cover, concentration in five products and one distributor, USD 1,784 million of principal due across 2028 and 2029 against USD 1,280 million of liquidity, claims outside the debt figure such as the USD 315 million royalty liability, and an intangible-heavy balance sheet.

fields.value: - Opportunities that could improve credit quality: the Befrena ramp-up and the international rollout of Credelio Quattro and Zenrelia, Elanco Ascend savings of USD 200 million to USD 250 million by 2030, leverage below 3x enabling an early refinancing, and a 25 basis point cut in the 2028 notes' interest rate after a fourth-quarter 2025 rating upgrade, which shows that pricing responds to credit quality.

fields.value: - Threats that could weaken credit quality: broader generic entry against Seresto and Advantage Family, a distributor changing volumes, Zenrelia label or litigation outcomes, shareholder returns once leverage falls and an unhedged floating-rate position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is average and improving, with leverage the weakest part. Scale is treated as average because last-twelve-months revenue of USD 5,020 million cannot be compared with peers, none being supplied. Competitive advantage is average, resting on approvals and patents for new franchises and weaker for off-patent products. Business diversification is balanced by end market and geography but concentrated by product and distributor. Cost and capex flexibility is limited in the short run by selling and research costs and partly discretionary capital spending, and margin stability is average, with gross margin of 57.79% in the half-year and clear operating leverage in both directions.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09; calculation C07; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is average and improving, at USD 379 million over the last twelve months. Liquidity is adequate to 2028 at USD 1,280 million, and the ability to refinance is the open question: the quarterly report says a rating upgrade in the fourth quarter of 2025 reduced the 2028 notes' interest rate, which is 25 basis points lower than at the 2025 year-end although the timing is not explained, but the rate also moves up with downgrades, the last in April 2023, and no rating report is supplied. Financial policy is creditor-aligned in behaviour and unproven in capacity. The trend is improving: net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 5.14x at 2025-12-31 (5.25x pro forma for the USD 76 million of AHV cash paid on 2026-04-30, with net debt of USD 3,548 million) to 4.38x at 2026-06-30, and adjusted net leverage fell by 0.50x in the half-year to 3.36x, although the adjusted year-end figure pro forma for AHV is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are balanced end markets, launch-led volume growth, light scheduled principal to 2028 and creditor-aligned behaviour; the main constraints are leverage, concentration, the 2028 and 2029 maturities and claims outside the debt figure. The key missing datapoints are the covenant calculation, the credit agreement and indenture, rating reports, ownership percentages, peer figures, last-twelve-months cash interest and the third-quarter 2026 report.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Short term, over 12 to 24 months, deleveraging should continue in 2026 and then meet the Seresto patent expiry and the 2028 refinancing. The issuer guides 2026 revenue to USD 5,090 million to USD 5,140 million and adjusted EBITDA to USD 1,010 million to USD 1,035 million, raised from USD 955 million to USD 985 million in February, with year-end net leverage of about 3.0x on its own definition against 3.1x to 3.3x in February; guidance implies slower second-half growth than the first half, restructuring savings add about USD 25 million in 2026 and USD 60 million in 2027, about USD 60 million of deferred AHV cash is due in January 2027, and the 2028 notes come within twelve months of maturity in August 2027. The credit implication is that 2027 carries three events at once: the patent expiry, the AHV payment and the refinancing window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium term, over three to five years, obligations accumulate while savings remain targets. The 2028 and 2029 maturities total USD 1,784 million, the headquarters lease option of USD 250 million falls in 2030, AHV contingent payments of up to USD 140 million run to 2032, and royalty cash is diverted to the buyer until August 2033, while Elanco Ascend savings of USD 200 million to USD 250 million by 2030 and the innovation revenue target of USD 1,250 million are management estimates. The December 2025 Investor Day outlook adds at least USD 1,000 million of free cash flow over 2026 to 2028 and a long-term leverage target of 2.0x to 2.5x, which would cover 56.05% of the 2028 and 2029 maturities if fully retained. Credit quality over this period depends on whether launches and savings outrun these claims.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-02-24_elanco-12312025exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C03; calculation C15; calculation C20; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tailwinds support revenue, margin and deleveraging. At sector level, management expects a sustainable mid-single-digit growth rate in animal health, which is a management view; at company level, volume growth of 7%, price of 2%, a revenue tailwind of about USD 60 million from currency in 2026 and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.9% against 21.2% a year earlier improve cash flow visibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_elanco-20260630exhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C08; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Headwinds pressure revenue, cash flow and refinancing confidence. At sector level, generic competition, antibiotic restrictions, pet-owner finances and tariffs weigh on pricing and volumes; at company level, Seresto erosion, distributor concentration, restructuring and AHV cash, selling cost growth of 12.01% and a swap roll that leaves floating-rate debt unhedged raise the risk that leverage reduction slows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_elan-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_elan-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C06; calculation C05; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside is issuer-specific and runs through the 2027 flea-and-tick season. The initiating condition is broader generic competition against Seresto, whose United States formulation patent expires in September 2027 after a generic competitor began selling in January 2026, together with price pressure on the Advantage Family products that already lack patent protection. The first operational break is rebates and discounts needed to hold distributor and retailer shelf space and volume growth falling from 7% towards the 2% price effect, on a parasiticide base of USD 593 million of half-year revenue for these two brands, Seresto and the Advantage Family.

Gross profit is 57.79% of revenue and selling costs rose 12.01% in the half-year, so lost revenue falls through close to the gross margin, adjusted EBITDA falls below the run rate of USD 388 million to USD 413 million that guidance implies for the second half of 2026, and free cash flow, which must also pay the USD 86 million restructuring reserve and the USD 100 million of deferred AHV cash, falls below USD 379 million. fields.value: The liquidity and refinancing consequence is the point of vulnerability. Liquidity of USD 1,280 million stays flat at best while USD 1,236 million falls due in 2028, the 2028 notes become a current liability within twelve months from August 2027, and refinancing would be attempted in a weaker market with an interest rate that moves up with downgrades. The evidence does not support a default path: scheduled principal is USD 63 million a year until 2028 and last-twelve-months free cash flow covers it 6.02x, so the supported outcome is higher refinancing cost and slower deleveraging, with liquidity distress avoided through 2028 if the revolver of USD 750 million remains available. Management levers are discretionary capital spending, selling and research costs, the restructuring and Ascend savings, withholding acquisitions, additional securitization capacity of about USD 165 million and early refinancing; there is no dividend to cut. The observable triggers are first-half 2027 Seresto and Pet Health volume, year-on-year adjusted EBITDA growth, and whether the 2028 maturities are addressed by the third-quarter 2027 report.

fields.value: Overall, Elanco presents an adequate business profile supported by balanced pet and livestock revenue, launch-led volume growth and creditor-aligned behaviour, but credit quality is constrained by adjusted net leverage of 3.36x, concentration in a few products and one distributor, and claims outside the debt figure. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 379 million over the last twelve months and light scheduled principal to 2028, although interest cover is flat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding parasiticide earnings through the 2027 generic season and on market access for USD 1,236 million due in 2028. The primary downside path is generic erosion of Seresto and Advantage Family earnings coinciding with that refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, rating reports, peer figures and the third-quarter 2026 report. Whether the business profile is better or worse than typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peers are supplied, and the financial profile trend is improving.
